title: Leaf fall: the retune reaches one of the four species the world now sows
question: Which floor do you want — B (what is landed now) or C (the same cut applied to conifer, shrub and creeper too)? If C is too bare, say so and I will take the other three part-way instead.
context_md:
Your lever was *"leaves are just falling too fast"*, and the cut you picked (**"C is best"**, card `20260823T161006584Z-6ecbab`) went into `tree`.

Since then `main` gained the flora-sowing work, and worlds now sow **four** woody species — creeper, shrub, conifer, tree — each into its own country. All four establish in 8 of 8 seeds. The cut is still only on `tree`, so **three of the four still shed at the old rate**.

That is why the win shrank: on the pre-merge world the retune measured **-72%** soil-writing decay. On today's world, the same edit measures **-42%** (A→B below). Roughly half the floor manufacture that is left after your retune comes from the three species it never touched (B→C is a further -48%).

One binary per arm (assets are compiled in), same scene, same seed, same 12,000 frames — four samples at 3,000 / 6,000 / 9,000 / 12,000.

**What I am unsure about, and why I am asking rather than just doing it:** living tissue *rises* as leaf fall slows (28.8k → 30.2k → 33.4k cells), because leaves that are not shed stay on the plant. C is the least floor and the most foliage. I cannot tell by eye whether C's crowns still read as separate stands or start to look like one mass — that is your call, not a number I have.

Ignore the frame timings on these runs; a sweep was running on the same box and they are not clean.
